The Stratospheric Controlled Perturbation Experiment (SCoPEx), proposed by Harvard University, aimed to investigate the behavior of small aerosol particles in the stratosphere. Spearheaded by Frank Keutsch, the project was introduced at the American Geophysical Union Fall Meeting in 2017 and focused on improving computer models to assess the risks and benefits of solar geoengineering, specifically solar radiation management. Importantly, SCoPEx was not intended for actual deployment of geoengineering techniques or to cool the planet.

The experiment planned to use a scientific balloon gondola at an altitude of approximately 20 km to release 100 grams to 2 kilograms of calcium carbonate. However, a 2021 test in Sweden was limited to hardware evaluation, with no particles released, following guidance from the SCoPEx Advisory Committee to pause for societal engagement. In March 2024, Harvard announced that Keutsch would discontinue SCoPEx and redirect the platform towards unrelated stratospheric research, marking a shift in focus for the project.
